text.p: Here are highlights from Friday morning's Swiss newspapers:

- Swiss steel producer Von Moos cancels its merger agreement with Von Roll, another major Swiss steel maker. The Lucerne-based Von Moos goup accused Von Roll of having given incorrect details about the company.
- Italian president Oscar Luigi Scalfaro traveled to the French-speaking part of Switzerland, where he visited the Federal Insitute of Techology in Lausanne.
- Swiss textile machine manufacturer Rieter plans to axe 700 jobs until summer next year - 300 in Switzerland and 400 in Germany.

- The free-trade project between the U.S. and Switzerland is on hold. The Swiss-American Chamber of Commerce, which supports the project, said it hoped negotiations could begin after the presidential elections in the U.S.

- The Swiss government said it would prepare a declaration that Switzerland is willing to investigate accusations that Swiss banks are still holding considerable amounts of gold which originated from the Nazi regime.
- Swiss underwear maker Schiesser plans to close down several manufacturing sites in Germany. Some 800 job will go.
